sources: dossier=named-lock.md Required-behaviors 'Counting-limit predicate is state=active' (2026-05-17, artifact) + Corrections-and-restorations 'CountByNamedLock predicate flip' entry naming state-based counting as intent, superseding the earlier 2026-05-04 'joined against' language per the dossier's own recency rule; doc=concepts/named-lock.md invariant 2 (pre-edit) said 'active node-runs joined against their claim-handle rows'; code=CountByNamedLock is a single-table SELECT count(*) filtered on the handle's own state='active' column, no join, matching the later-dated dossier entry.
note: The dossier explicitly documents a 2026-05-17 correction to state-based (non-join) counting as intent, which is later than and supersedes the 2026-05-04 join-based phrasing also present in the dossier; the doc's invariant 2 still used the superseded join language. Rewrote to describe the single-table state='active' count.

sources: dossier=named-lock.md is silent on whether advisory-lock's per-name serialization must be named inside named-lock's own Invariants section (it appears only as an Adjacent slug in Boundaries); doc=concepts/named-lock.md Boundaries lists advisory-lock as Adjacent only; code=runner_acquire.go takeNamedAdvisoryLocks/TakeNamedLockInTx serializes count-then-insert in runner_acquire_named_locks.go, a real correctness dependency not restated in named-lock's Invariants.
note: User ruling 2026-07-17 (design-call resolved, option A): named-lock.md's Invariants now explicitly declare the dependency on concept:advisory-lock's per-name in-tx serialization for capacity-counting correctness — mechanism ownership stays with advisory-lock; the dependent concept names the dependency so a future weakening is grep-discoverable. Doc updated; no code change.

sources: dossier=named-lock.md does not itself discuss annotation practice; corroborated instead by root CLAUDE.md ('Concept-to-code links — grep -rn @concept: . in source') and .ok-planner/CLAUDE.md's description of @concept: as marking 'where a concept is enforced or expressed'; doc=concepts/named-lock.md is unaffected (defect is in code, not doc); code=grep '@concept: named-lock' over lib/cmd/test/tools returns zero matches despite active enforcement sites (capacity gate, named delete, lock ordering, limit validation, undeclared-lock registration rejection).
note: Two independent repo-wide artifacts (root CLAUDE.md and the .ok-planner meta-doc) agree that @concept: anchors mark load-bearing enforcement sites for a concept, and named-lock has clear, multi-site enforcement code with zero anchors anywhere. This is a code-side traceability gap, not a doc defect; queued as fix-code, not touched.

sources: dossier=publisher.md Required-behaviors (2026-06-11, last-mile-stability, artifact, cited) states only 'retry-forever reconciliation' with no backoff qualifier for the Subscribe-reconciliation mechanism; the 'with backoff' phrase appears only in the dossier's uncited Net-position summary and is contradicted by the cited 2026-05-17 backoff entry, which is scoped to a different mechanism (publisher-side POST retry, not rimsky's Subscribe reconciliation); doc=concepts/publisher.md invariant (pre-edit) claimed the reconciliation worker has 'backoff and no attempt cap'; code=reconcileMountingSubscriptionsOnce (lib/runtime/publishers.go) runs on a flat time.NewTicker cadence with no exponential backoff and no cap; pow28 backoff exists only in callSubscribeWithRetry/callListSubscriptionsWithRetry, used solely by startup resync and capped at subscribeRetryAttempts=3.
note: No real path has both properties the doc claims together; resolved by folding this into the row-545 DRY fix, which removes the restated mechanism detail from publisher.md entirely and defers wholly to concept:publisher-subscription, eliminating the inaccurate restatement rather than asserting a specific cadence claim in a second doc.

sources: dossier=intent/host-agent-proxy.md (2026-06-13, c41b7afe, transcript): 'the ServiceName interceptor on the lifecycle, publisher, validation, and data-processing dial paths' uses 'dial path' to mean the outbound RPC client rimsky uses to call a peer service, i.e. the same thing publisher.md's Boundaries already names 'the peer client'; doc=concepts/publisher.md Owns list (pre-edit) listed both 'the peer client' and 'the operator dial path' as if distinct; code=PublisherClient (lib/runtime/publishers.go) is the single outbound dial/RPC client used for Capabilities/Subscribe/Unsubscribe/ListSubscriptions, with no separate 'operator dial' construct.
note: A transcript-sourced dossier entry from an adjacent concept independently confirms 'dial path' names the peer RPC client, already covered by 'the peer client' in the same Owns list; 'operator dial path' was a redundant, ambiguously-worded duplicate (compounded by 'operator' meaning something else earlier in the same doc). Removed the redundant item.

sources: dossier=publisher.md itself names concept:publisher-subscription as 'the rimsky<->publisher binding lifecycle' in Adjacent, and publisher-subscription.md's own Boundaries Owns the lifecycle state field and carries the full mechanism description; doc=concepts/publisher.md invariant (pre-edit) restated the reconciliation-worker mechanism in detail with only a failed-state-scoped citation to concept:publisher-subscription; code confirms the mechanism (reconcileMountingSubscriptionsOnce) lives in one place and the two docs were describing the same code from two sites.
note: The concept split (publisher.md Adjacent-cites publisher-subscription as lifecycle owner; publisher-subscription.md Owns the lifecycle state field and already carries the full, current invariant text) makes publisher.md's detailed restatement a DRY violation with a citation scoped too narrowly. Replaced the restated mechanism with a single sentence deferring reconciliation, cadence, and failed-state ownership wholly to concept:publisher-subscription; this is the same edit that resolves row 543.

sources: dossier=role-template.md Net-position/Intentional-absences (2026-05-15, control-plane-mcp-and-auth, artifact): 'Operators add custom roles via local role files, not any server surface' and 'Server surface for custom roles: custom roles are local role files only' — no per-user directory mechanism claimed anywhere; doc=concepts/role-template.md (pre-edit) claimed a 'per-user roles directory' scan in addition to a role-file flag; code=loadRole (cmd/rimsky/cli/auth_common.go) only reads an explicit --role-file path or the embedded bundled-role FS; grep for any roles-dir/XDG/home-directory scan returns nothing.
note: The dossier consistently describes custom roles as 'local role files' passed explicitly, never a directory-scan mechanism, and code implements only the explicit-file path. The doc's directory-loader claim was fabricated relative to both intent and code; corrected to describe the role-file flag only.

sources: dossier=role-template.md does not describe the key-detail display's matching behavior in any required-behavior entry (silent on the exact mechanism); doc=concepts/role-template.md invariant (pre-edit) gave the illustrative display example 'role:operator + 1 override', implying a partial-match-with-overrides display; code=matchRole (cmd/rimsky/cli/auth_list.go) does exact-match only via grantsEqual, returning 'role:'+name on an exact match or 'custom' otherwise — no partial-match/override-counting display path exists.
note: The dossier is silent on the specific display algorithm, but design docs are current-state-only and the illustrative example describes a feature (partial match with an override count) that provably does not exist in code; corrected the example to describe the real exact-match-or-custom behavior.

sources: dossier=role-template.md Net-position (2026-05-15): 'These ship embedded in the CLI binary' — silent on load timing beyond embedding, so no dossier entry claims startup loading; doc=concepts/role-template.md (pre-edit) said templates 'are loaded at startup'; code=roles/embed.go uses //go:embed for compile-time inclusion and Load(name) is called lazily by each auth subcommand (auth_create.go/auth_list.go/auth_init.go call sites), never at process startup.
note: The dossier only claims compile-time embedding, not startup loading; code confirms lazy, per-command reads with nothing executed at process startup. Folded into the same paragraph edit as row 556: replaced 'loaded at startup' with 'read on demand when a command needs them.'
